```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## Load Required Libraries

```{r load-libraries}
library(edgeR)
library(ggplot2)
library(Biostrings)  # For working with FASTA files
library(plotly)  # For interactive PCA plotting
```

## Load Count Matrix

```{r load-data}
# Load the count matrix
data <- read.table("/Users/oliver/Desktop/RNASeq_2025/FeatureCounts_w_brakerGTF/home/newol210/macknight_oliver/featureCounts_working_dir_braker_annotations/featureCounts_fastpProcessed_17_samples_UTMhap1_counts_fraction_brakerGTF.txt",
                   header = TRUE, row.names = 1, sep = "\t", check.names = FALSE, comment.char = "#")

# Remove specific columns (e.g., columns 2, 3, 4, and 5)
data <- data[, -c(1:5)]

# Ensure counts are numeric and round fractional counts to integers
counts <- as.matrix(data)
counts <- round(counts)

# Remove genes with zero counts across all samples
counts <- counts[rowSums(counts) > 0, ]

# Define sample groups
colnames(counts) <- gsub("\\./|_Aligned\\.sortedByCoord\\.out\\.bam", "", colnames(counts))

group_labels <- ifelse(grepl("^N", colnames(counts)), "None", 
                ifelse(grepl("^L", colnames(counts)), "Low", 
                ifelse(grepl("^H", colnames(counts)), "High", NA)))
```

## Perform 2D PCA Analysis

```{r 2D pca-analysis}
# Convert raw counts to log-CPM
logCPM <- cpm(counts, log=TRUE)

# Perform PCA
pca <- prcomp(t(logCPM), scale. = TRUE)

# Create a data frame for plotting
pca_data <- data.frame(
  PC1 = pca$x[,1],
  PC2 = pca$x[,2],
  Group = group_labels
)

# Plot 2D PCA
p <- plot_ly(
  pca_data,
  x = ~PC1,
  y = ~PC2,
  color = ~Group,
  colors = c("#5A3175", "#AA76D1", "green"),
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers"
) %>%
  layout(
    title = "STAR alignment FeatureCounts UTMhap1 reference",
    xaxis = list(title = "PC1"),
    yaxis = list(title = "PC2")
  )

p  # Display the plot

# Boxplot of explained variation in first 3 PCs
boxplot(
  pca$x[,1:3],
  main = "PCA Component Variance",
  col = c("blue", "green", "red")
)
```

## Perform 3D PCA Analysis

```{r pca-analysis}
# Convert raw counts to log-CPM
logCPM <- cpm(counts, log=TRUE)

# Perform PCA
pca <- prcomp(t(logCPM), scale. = TRUE)

# Create a data frame for plotting
pca_data <- data.frame(PC1 = pca$x[,1], PC2 = pca$x[,2], PC3 = pca$x[,3], Group = group_labels)

# Plot 3D PCA
p <- plot_ly(pca_data, x = ~PC1, y = ~PC2, z = ~PC3, color = ~Group, colors = c("#5A3175", "#AA76D1", "green")) %>%
  add_markers(marker = list(size = 5)) %>%
  layout(title = "STAR alignment FeatureCounts UTMhap1 reference", scene = list(xaxis = list(title = "PC1"),
                                             yaxis = list(title = "PC2"),
                                             zaxis = list(title = "PC3")))

p  # Display the 3D plot
boxplot(pca$x[,1:3], main="PCA Component Variance", col=c("blue", "green", "red"))
```

```{r check PC1 loadings}
head(sort(abs(pca$rotation[,1]), decreasing = TRUE), 20)
```

```{r check PC2 loadings}
head(sort(abs(pca$rotation[,2]), decreasing = TRUE), 20)
```

```{r visualize the top contributing genes for each principal component (PC)}
# Set the number of top genes to display
top_n <- 10  

# Extract the top contributing genes for PC1, PC2, and PC3
top_genes_PC1 <- head(sort(abs(pca$rotation[,1]), decreasing = TRUE), top_n)
top_genes_PC2 <- head(sort(abs(pca$rotation[,2]), decreasing = TRUE), top_n)
top_genes_PC3 <- head(sort(abs(pca$rotation[,3]), decreasing = TRUE), top_n)

# Convert to data frames for plotting
df_PC1 <- data.frame(Gene = names(top_genes_PC1), Contribution = top_genes_PC1, PC = "PC1")
df_PC2 <- data.frame(Gene = names(top_genes_PC2), Contribution = top_genes_PC2, PC = "PC2")
df_PC3 <- data.frame(Gene = names(top_genes_PC3), Contribution = top_genes_PC3, PC = "PC3")

# Combine into a single data frame
df_pca_loadings <- rbind(df_PC1, df_PC2, df_PC3)

# Plot loadings as a barplot using ggplot2
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(df_pca_loadings, aes(x = reorder(Gene, Contribution), y = Contribution, fill = PC)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  coord_flip() +  # Flip for better readability
  facet_wrap(~ PC, scales = "free_y") +  # Separate plots for PC1, PC2, PC3
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Top Contributing Genes for PC1, PC2, and PC3",
       x = "Gene",
       y = "Contribution") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("PC1" = "#5A3175", "PC2" = "#AA76D1", "PC3" = "#1B6B2A"))  # Custom colors
```


## Create DGEList Object

```{r dge-object}
# Subset counts to include only "None" and "High" samples
valid_groups <- group_labels %in% c("None", "Low")
counts <- counts[, valid_groups, drop = FALSE]
groups <- factor(group_labels[valid_groups])

# Create DGEList object
dge <- DGEList(counts = counts, group = groups)

# Filter out lowly expressed genes
keep <- filterByExpr(dge)
dge <- dge[keep, , keep.lib.sizes = FALSE]

# Normalize library sizes
dge <- calcNormFactors(dge, method = "TMM")

# Normalized CPM for heatmaps, plots, reports
norm_counts <- cpm(dge, normalized.lib.sizes = TRUE)
```

## Estimate Dispersion

```{r estimate-dispersion}
# Estimate dispersion
dge <- estimateDisp(dge)
```

## Perform Differential Expression Analysis

```{r differential-expression}
# Perform exact test
dge_results <- exactTest(dge, pair = c("None", "Low"))

dge_table <- topTags(dge_results, n = Inf)$table
significant_genes <- dge_table[dge_table$FDR < 0.005 & abs(dge_table$logFC) > 1, ]
```


## Plot Results

```{r plot-volcano}
# Volcano plot
volcano_data <- significant_genes  # Only plot significant genes
volcano_data$negLogFDR <- -log10(volcano_data$FDR)

# Select top 10 genes with highest -log10(FDR) and logFC for labeling
top_genes <- volcano_data[order(-volcano_data$negLogFDR, -abs(volcano_data$logFC)), ][1:10, ]

# Plot volcano
ggplot(volcano_data, aes(x = logFC, y = negLogFDR)) +
  geom_point(color = "red") +
  geom_text(data = top_genes, aes(label = rownames(top_genes)), vjust = -1, size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Volcano Plot (Significant Genes)", x = "Log2 Fold Change", y = "-Log10(FDR)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r save-results}
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = TRUE, col.names = NA)
```

## Extract Significant Gene Sequences

```{r extract-dna-sequences}
# Load significant gene IDs
sig_genes <- rownames(significant_genes)

# Read the fasta file
fasta_file <- "/Users/oliver/Desktop/RNASeq_2025/FeatureCounts_w_brakerGTF/"  # Path to your fasta file
fasta <- readDNAStringSet(fasta_file)

# Filter fasta sequences to match significant genes
filtered_fasta <- fasta[names(fasta) %in% sig_genes]

# Save the filtered fasta to a specific location
output_fasta <- "/Users/oliver/Desktop/R_edegeR_RNASeq/filtered_DEGs_low_vs_high.fasta"  # Replace with your desired path
writeXStringSet(filtered_fasta, filepath = output_fasta)

cat("Filtered sequences saved to:", output_fasta, "\n")

# Write filtered fasta headers to a text file
headers_file <- "/Users/oliver/Desktop/R_edegeR_RNASeq/filtered_fasta_headers.txt"
writeLines(names(filtered_fasta), headers_file)
cat("Filtered fasta headers saved to:", headers_file, "\n")
```

```{r extract-protein-sequences}
# Load significant gene IDs
sig_genes <- rownames(significant_genes)

# Read the fasta file
fasta_file <- "/Users/oliver/Desktop/RNASeq_2025/FeatureCounts_w_brakerGTF/braker_asterisks_removed.aa.fasta"  # Path to your fasta file
fasta <- readAAStringSet(fasta_file)

# Filter fasta sequences to match significant genes
filtered_fasta <- fasta[names(fasta) %in% sig_genes]

# Save the filtered fasta to a specific location
output_fasta <- "/Users/oliver/Desktop/RNASeq_2025/FeatureCounts_w_brakerGTF/filtered_sequences_low_vs_high.fasta"  # Replace with your desired path

# Create directory if it doesn't exist
dir.create(dirname(output_fasta), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Write filtered fasta
writeXStringSet(filtered_fasta, filepath = output_fasta)

cat("Filtered sequences saved to:", output_fasta, "\n")

# Write filtered fasta headers to a text file
headers_file <- "/Users/oliver/Desktop/RNASeq_2025/FeatureCounts_w_brakerGTF/filtered_low_vs_high_fasta_headers.txt"
writeLines(names(filtered_fasta), headers_file)
cat("Filtered fasta headers saved to:", headers_file, "\n")
```

## Verify Headers Match Significant Genes

```{r verify-headers}
# Load filtered fasta headers
fasta_headers <- readLines("/Users/oliver/Desktop/R_edegeR_RNASeq/filtered_fasta_headers.txt")

# Load significant genes
significant_genes_list <- rownames(significant_genes)

# Check for mismatches
mismatches <- setdiff(fasta_headers, significant_genes_list)

if (length(mismatches) == 0) {
  cat("All filtered fasta headers match significant genes.\n")
} else {
  cat("The following headers are mismatched or missing:\n")
  print(mismatches)
}
```

## Then you need to run the following command in terminal to append all eggNOG annotations (if present) to DEGs
# Note that I needed to manually edit the header of the eggNOG file before running this chunk so that it just contained the header starting with "query"
```{bash}
cd ~/Desktop/RNASeq_2025/FeatureCounts_w_brakerGTF

awk 'NR==FNR {a[$1]=$0; next} {print $0, ($1 in a ? "\t" a[$1] : "\tN/A")}' braker_asterisks_removed_aa_eggnog.emapper.annotations.txt significant_genes_none_vs_low_brakerGTF_inc2023_dataset_FDR_0.005.txt > significant_genes_none_vs_low_brakerGTF_inc2023_dataset_FDR_0.005_w_eggNOG_annotations.txt
```

## After this, I just used Excel to make a new text document with all the up-regulated transcript ID's and their corresponding GO terms
# Then use awk to remove rows from this new document that didn't have eggNOG-mapper annotations (GO terms)
```{bash}
awk -F'\t' '$2 != ""' input.txt > filtered_output.txt
```
